Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is 9to5Mac's weekly series that highlights the latest apps from the independent app scene. If you're a developer and want to get your app featured, reach out to us.

Farwave takes an interesting new approach to audio player apps by putting them around the globe. You can explore the world, finding radio stations from around the globe, complete with nice 3D visuals. For podcasts and music you want to listen to, you can also explore them with their own distinct visuals in the app.

Main features

Farwave lets you listen to every radio station around the world. You can spin the globe, find a region, and tap on a station. If you just want to listen to something random, there's also a "Take me anywhere" button. The app also offers a listening history so you can go back and listen to stations later.

In addition to radio, Farwave offers podcasts and music — each displayed on their own separate planets. You can search for podcasts or add their RSS feeds, and the app also supports playlists, adjustable speed, and offline downloads.

For music, it doesn't support Apple Music, but you can import your music files from a computer or the Files app. Each artist has their own signal, and music is stored on the device for offline playback.

Download the app

Farwave is available for free on the App Store for iPhone and iPad running iOS 18 or later. For the full experience, including podcasts, music import, and more, you can purchase FarWave Pro for $2.99 per month or $14.99 per year.
